ops.title: csops(CS_OPS_TEAMID) may be forgeable under validation category 6
ops.premise:
G1 asks: can internal/trust's kernel-only peer verifier trust CS_OPS_TEAMID (and
by extension CS_OPS_IDENTITY / the signing identifier) as a team-identity anchor,
or must it walk the certificate chain off the hot path?

PREMISE (falsifiable): A holder of ANY genuine Developer ID Application certificate
(team B) can craft a CodeDirectory whose teamID field declares a FOREIGN team (team A),
sign that CD's hash with team B's real private key, and the binary validates at the
kernel/AMFI level as CS_VALID + CS_VALIDATION_CATEGORY_DEVELOPER_ID (6) while
csops(CS_OPS_TEAMID) reports "team A". If true, a same-UID unix-socket peer verifier
that trusts CS_OPS_TEAMID alone is FORGEABLE by any Developer ID holder, and
internal/trust must add the design's cdhash-memoized off-handshake-path chain check
for the leaf-OU==teamID (and signing-identifier) clause. If false (the binary is
killed at exec, or reports the real team, or drops below category 6), kernel-only
ships as specified.

EVIDENCE SO FAR:
- Web research (primary-source read of xnu + Security.framework), high confidence:
  csblob_parse_teamid() in bsd/kern/ubc_subr.c reads teamID as a raw string at
  cd->teamOffset with NO certificate cross-check; kern_cs.c accessors return the
  cached string verbatim. The only OU==teamID check in Apple's published source is
  userspace Security.framework SecStaticCode::verifySignature() (errSecCSBadTeamIdentifier),
  on the Gatekeeper / codesign --verify path — NOT demonstrably in the AMFI exec-time
  path that sets CS_VALID and the validation category. Caveat: AMFI kext is closed
  source; cannot rule out an exec-time cross-check via amfid. No named CVE / public PoC.
- Local measurement T1 (real Developer ID sign, macOS 26.5.2): category 6,
  TEAMID="SXKCTF23Q2" (the real cert OU). T3 (byte-flip teamID of a finished binary):
  codesign --verify INVALID, process SIGKILLed (rc=137) at exec. NEITHER tested the
  re-sign attack — T1 used codesign (derives teamID from cert; a tooling courtesy,
  signer.cpp considerTeamID), T3 breaks the CD hash (wrong attack). The premise is
  UNTESTED by the local run and is the open question.

NEXT: run the decisive PoC — rcodesign sign --team-name <foreign> with the real
Developer ID cert, run it, read csops(CS_OPS_TEAMID) + CS_OPS_VALIDATION_CATEGORY.
This is the only thing that resolves whether amfid enforces OU==teamID at exec.
